notes: Coleman does NOT use usesStylesOf york: styles 1-2 match York's systems verbatim (same sample serials, same letter tables, same October 2004 boundary, charts note York UPG manufacturing), but styles 3-4 are Coleman-only numeric systems and the builder forbids styles alongside usesStylesOf. The month/year order swap is documented as a 1991/1992 boundary, not April 1992: style 4 (month first) ended 1991, style 3 (year first) began 1992. Dual-brand Coleman-Evcon history 1999-2005 is documented on the page. SHIPPED IN PHASE 2b: style-2 (1971 to October 2004, 4 letters + 6-digit sequence, sample WAKM011379 = January 1980 or 2001) via the dual-candidate schema extension; now IMAGE-CONFIRMED (image-pass Nov 8, see style-2 notes). Style-1 (after October 2004, 10-character serials, sample W0K5896070 = September 2005) is chart-verified and shipped (image-pass Nov 8); it is encoded from Coleman's own chart, not extrapolated from York.

styles.notes: Chart-verified (image-pass Nov 8): 2nd and 4th digits combine for the year ('0'+'5'='05' = 2005), 3rd character is the month letter (K = September on this chart). Plant table: A Apodaca, N Norman, S Source One, W Wichita. Began October 2004, York UPG manufacturing. The style-2 note's warning not to carry K=September into style 1 is moot: this chart also maps K to September.

IMAGE-CONFIRMED (image-pass Nov 8): Coleman's own style-2 chart matches these tables exactly (same sample WAKM011379, same dual-candidate year table, same month table). Month is 2nd letter, year is 3rd letter; I, O, Q, U, Z not used. Year codes repeat on a 21-year cycle, hence dual candidates. N=2004 is January-September 2004 only (post-2004 system from October 2004) -- recorded here, not expressible in the table. The style-1 chart also maps K to September, so the old warning against carrying K=September into style 1 is moot.

Year first, month second. yearFloor 1992 reflects the documented start year; with this floor, trying style-3 before style-4 resolves the numeric overlap: a 9-digit serial whose style-3 month field is invalid falls through to style-4, and a serial matching style-3 with year 1992 or later cannot be a style-4 serial (style-4 ended 1991).

Month first, year second: the reverse of style-3. DOCUMENTED-LENGTH DISCREPANCY: the page's style list shows a 9-digit sample (018812345) but the style-4 chart body shows 10 digits (0188123456, month 01, year 88, 6-digit sequence); the 10-digit body serial is used as the example and the pattern allows 9-10 digits. RESIDUAL EDGE, flagged not resolved: a 9-digit serial that fails style-3 month validation but passes style-4 with a year of 1992 or later would decode to a post-1991 year outside style-4's documented era; the schema has no era upper bound to reject it. No start date is documented for this style, so the default 1960 floor is kept.
